questions.question_text: Using the supplied booklet's vehicle-tax table in the teaching, determine the vehicle tax payable for a sedan with a tare weight of $1080\text{ kg}$ registered for private use.

options.why: Looked up the business use fee instead of the private use fee.
Used the weight category for vehicles up to $975\text{ kg}$.
Used the higher weight category for vehicles from $1155\text{ to } 1504\text{ kg}$.

questions.solution_text: A tare weight of $1080\text{ kg}$ falls in the range $976\text{ to } 1154\text{ kg}$. For private use, the vehicle tax is $\$295$.

questions.question_text: Using the supplied booklet's vehicle-tax table in the teaching, what is the vehicle tax payable for a truck with a tare weight of $1620\text{ kg}$ registered for business use?

options.why: Looked up the private use fee instead of the business use fee.
Used the weight bracket $1155\text{ to } 1504\text{ kg}$ instead of $1505\text{ to } 2504\text{ kg}$.
Used the lowest weight category up to $975\text{ kg}$ for business use.

questions.solution_text: A tare weight of $1620\text{ kg}$ falls in the range $1505\text{ to } 2504\text{ kg}$. For business use, the fee is $\$847$.

questions.question_text:
A driver receives a comprehensive car insurance quote of $\$1350$ and has earned a $30\%$ no-claim bonus.
How much is the driver required to pay?

options.why: Calculated the discount amount instead of the payable premium.
Added the $30\%$ bonus to the quote instead of subtracting it as a discount.
Applied a $10\%$ discount instead of the stated $30\%$ no-claim bonus.

questions.question_text:
A vehicle has a purchase price and market value of $\$24\,800$.
Using the supplied booklet's stamp-duty method, calculate the stamp duty payable.

options.why: Applied $5\%$ instead of $3\%$ to the value below the threshold.
Used $0.3\%$ instead of $3\%$.
Added the stamp duty to the vehicle price instead of reporting only the duty.

questions.question_text:
A vehicle has a purchase price and market value of $\$53\,600$.
Using the supplied booklet's stamp-duty method, calculate the stamp duty payable.

options.why: Applied a flat $3\%$ to the entire value.
Applied a flat $5\%$ to the entire value.
Calculated $5\%$ of the excess but omitted the $\$1350$ duty on the first $\$45\,000$.

questions.question_text:
A driver is quoted $\$1240$ for comprehensive car insurance and has a $25\%$ no-claim bonus.
Calculate the premium payable.

options.why: Reported the $25\%$ discount instead of the payable premium.
Added $25\%$ to the quoted premium instead of subtracting it.
Subtracted $\$25$ instead of $25\%$ of the premium.

questions.question_text:
A car with a tare weight of $1154\text{ kg}$ is registered for business use.
Using the supplied booklet's vehicle-tax table in the teaching, determine the vehicle tax payable.

options.why: Used the private use fee in the correct weight category.
Placed $1154\text{ kg}$ in the category starting at $1155\text{ kg}$.
Used the business use category for vehicles up to $975\text{ kg}$.

questions.solution_text:
$1154\text{ kg}$ is included in the range $976\text{ to } 1154\text{ kg}$.
The business use vehicle tax is $\$467$.

questions.question_text:
A vehicle has a purchase price and market value of $\$92\,750$.
Using the supplied booklet's stamp-duty method, calculate the stamp duty payable.

options.why: Applied $3\%$ to the entire value instead of using $5\%$ on the excess.
Applied $5\%$ to the entire value instead of only the excess above $\$45\,000$.
Calculated only $5\%$ of the excess and omitted the $\$1350$ duty on the first $\$45\,000$.
